trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out up or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Number 2 is only reachable this way.
The line must go down: up is number 6, which comes later.
I can't rule out right or up yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.
Going right would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up.
Cell (5,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going right, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,5). So the line goes up.
Going left would force the line onto number 6 before its turn. So the line goes up.
Going up would cut off the top-left corner (6 cells). So the line goes left.
Cell (3,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going right would force the line onto number 8 before its turn. So the line goes down.
The line must go right: down is number 9, which comes later.
Cell (1,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going down would strand number 9: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (6,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
